pop_table <- read.table(path_resrepo("data/raw/data_input/Madagascar_Borneo.poptable"), sep = "\t", fill = TRUE)
colnames(pop_table) <- c("IID", "V2","FID","Population","V5","V6","V7")

#Remove the "RR"
mad_bor_g1000_sum_fam$id <- sub("RR.*", "", mad_bor_g1000_sum_fam$id)
mad_bor_g1000_sum_fam$V2 <- sub("RR.*", "", mad_bor_g1000_sum_fam$V2)

#Find Malagasy entries 
pop_table_sub <- subset(pop_table,pop_table$IID %in% mad_bor_g1000_sum_fam$id)

#match up the ID's with pop table metadata
matching_m <- match(mad_bor_g1000_sum_fam$id, pop_table_sub$IID)

mad_bor_g1000_sum_fam$population <- ifelse(!is.na(matching_m), pop_table_sub$Population[matching_m], mad_bor_g1000_sum_fam$population)


# replace any _ with a space
#mad_bor_g1000_sum_fam$population <- gsub("_", " ", mad_bor_g1000_sum_fam$population)

# replace any " " in $populaiton with a "_"
mad_bor_g1000_sum_fam$population <- gsub(" ", "_", mad_bor_g1000_sum_fam$population)

# any $id begining GRC has $population "Sumba"
mad_bor_g1000_sum_fam$population[grepl("^GRC", mad_bor_g1000_sum_fam$id)] <- "Sumba"

#mad_bor_g1000_sum_fam$id <- as.numeric(rownames(mad_bor_g1000_sum_fam))
mad_bor_g1000_sum_fam$population <- as.factor(mad_bor_g1000_sum_fam$population)

#mad_bor_g1000_sum_fam$V6 <- mad_bor_g1000_sum_fam$population
write.table(mad_bor_g1000_sum_fam, resrepo::path_resrepo("data/intermediate/rbind_data/mad_bor_g1000_sum.fam"), row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE, sep = " ", quote = FALSE)

# Write a test bash script for ALDER

mindis: 0.005 - minimum genetic distance (in Morgans) at which to start curve fitting (default: determined using LD correlation). 
https://comppopgenworkshop2019.readthedocs.io/en/latest/contents/06_alder/alder.html 
States that the default calculates the correlation in LD decay between the target and each reference, and uses 'the minimum distance that shows no correlation in both references.' 
'If it continues beyond 2 cM (due to either a strong bottleneck or admixture in a reference), the program aborts.'
In example with Merina as Target and Esan and Borneo as reference, setting mindis to default causes the program to abort.
jackknife: YES - outputs results from leave-one-chromosome-out jackknifing

For now, using checkmap: NO - why does our map have an issue?
binsize: 0.0005 default - genetic distance resolution (in Morgans) - the size of bins that ALDER splits the genome up into, used to calculate the distance between the bins of two snps as opposed to the distance between the each individual pair of snps, for computational efficiency 

# Run bash script

```{bash}
cd ~/Git/malagasy_diversity/code
alder -p s11b_alder_merina.par > s11b_alder_merina.log
```

# Example plot 

Using https://comppopgenworkshop2019.readthedocs.io/en/latest/contents/06_alder/alder.html 

E[Y] = M times e^-nd + K

```{r}
fn1 = "../results/s11_ALDER/alder_merina.txt"

n = 25.17    ## decay parameter - the estimate for admixture date
M = 0.00153897  ## amp_exp
K = 0.00040424  ## amp_aff

d1 = read.table(fn1, header = F)
d1 <- d1[-nrow(d1),]
colnames(d1) = c("Dist", "weightedLD", "npairs")
xv = as.vector(d1$Dist)        ## distance between SNP bins (cM)
yv = as.vector(d1$weightedLD)  ## Weighted LD
#fv = as.vector(d1$use) == "Y"  ## a boolean vector marking if each bin is used in fitting
prdv = M * exp(-1 * n * xv / 100) + K # E[Y] = M times e^-nd + K

dev.new()
plot(xv, yv, xlab="Genetic distance (cM)", ylab = "weighted LD", pch=4, col="blue")
points(xv, prdv, type="l", lwd=1.5, col="red")
```

The middle and right columns show the date estimate (B, E, H) and amplitude (C, F, I) as a function of d0.
